## 2026-11-08 - Signal paths: fade with distance, slower smooth pulses, softer glow
- Asked: paths to signals fade out with distance until completely invisible at a third of a solar system's
  distance; out of that range signals don't show on the minimap either; the pulses moving along the paths slower
  and smoother; the paths' glow a smoother gradient.
- ShipScanner.signal_range(): a third of the system across - twice the farthest gate / station / planet from the
  star, / 3 (Atrapos: 7,333); worked out once per system (not cached until the system is built).
- _draw_paths: every point of a path fades with its distance from your ship (full to 30 % of the range, gone at
  the range - drawn no further), and so do its nodes, pulses and the rings at the signal (none beyond range). The
  glow is now six fine layers (46 to 7 px, faintest first) under a 3 px core and a 1.2 px white-hot line - a smooth
  falloff. Pulses glide on the curve itself (were snapped to its points) at 0.12 of the path a second (was 0.45),
  with a short soft tail, easing in from the ship; the rings pulse slower too. Paths sampled every 30 px (was 40).
- Minimap._draw_signals: signals beyond signal_range() aren't drawn (no diamond, no rim arrow).
- Tests: test_signals 7/7, test_scanner pass.
- Files: scripts/ship_scanner.gd, scripts/minimap.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Skylla, the sea witch: the monster signal's new creature
- Asked: use the latest two images in Downloads (ed47906f... - the full monster; 6dd1ba19... - split into the
  upper body and the tentacles) to recreate the monster as a procedural sprite in the game, easy to animate, its
  tentacles and arms animated; use it for the signal with the monster scenario.
- SeaWitch (scripts/sea_witch.gd, new; extends SpaceMonster - keeps its bullet-hell attacks): drawn in code, part
  by part, in the reference's colours with an ink / shade / body / highlight cel style, all from round strokes
  (capsules, circles, ellipses - no polygon a tight curl can fold):
  - 8 magenta tentacles (spread down, out and a little up behind her), each a 22-point spine with a travelling
    wave and a tip curling outward; shaded underside, lit top, pink sucker rings all along the underside.
  - The upper body: neck, torso from overlapping ellipses (shoulders, ribcage, waist, hips), a shaped gold
    breastplate with straps and a gem, a gold greek-key belt where she rises from the tentacles.
  - Arms with shoulder, elbow and wrist: a gold armband and a greek-key bracer each; hands with four clawed fingers
    that flex. Idle: out and down, swaying; charging an attack they swing forward and up, hands meeting in front of
    her, where the energy gathers (mouth() = 0.66 x length ahead).
  - Head: pointed ears, gold earrings, slanted red glowing eyes that track you and blink, a snarling mouth that
    opens wider as she charges, the gold laurel crown with a gem; a storm of indigo hair curls (32) with spiral
    highlights, swaying.
  - A magenta halo, brighter as she charges.
- EnemyTypes.MONSTERS "skylla" (look "sea_witch"; hull 1050, length 380, keeps 560 away); Enemy creates a SeaWitch
  for look "sea_witch". The monster signal now spawns Skylla (texts updated); the Void Leviathan type stays (old
  saves).
- Docs: game.md (the bio-signature encounter). Tests: test_signals (the monster is a SeaWitch named Skylla) 8/8.
- Files: new scripts/sea_witch.gd; scripts/enemy_types.gd, enemy.gd, signal_site.gd, data/docs/game.md,
  tests/test_signals.gd

## 2026-11-08 - Skylla traced from the reference art itself
- Asked: the monster didn't look like the reference images - be far more precise and detailed, carefully trace the
  image keeping all the details, shapes, colours and outlines.
- The drawn-in-code sea witch is replaced by the art itself, cut into animatable parts:
  - tools/skylla_parts.py (new; runs in the art venv ~/.local/share/space-atrapos-art/venv: rembg, opencv,
    scipy): removes the background of external/images/skylla/skylla_parts.png (the reference, copied there with
    skylla_assembled.png) with rembg's isnet-anime model, takes its two shapes (upper body, tentacle cluster), cuts
    each arm from the body at the shoulder and again at the elbow (polygons / lines traced on the art), and writes
    data/sprites/monster_skylla_{tentacles,torso,left_upper,left_fore,right_upper,right_fore}.png (48 px margins)
    plus monster_skylla.json (crop origins, shoulders, elbows, eyes, mouth, tentacle hub and their layout shift:
    140 px higher under her, as in the assembled picture).
  - SeaWitch (scripts/sea_witch.gd, rewritten): a rig of those sprites (art scale = length x 1.8 / 1100). The
    tentacles writhe in shaders/skylla_tentacles.gdshader (each pixel taken from a little way along its
    tentacle - waves running out, a slow coil, the tips swaying up to 26 art px, the roots holding); her hair
    drifts in shaders/skylla_hair.gdshader (nothing below the crown moves); arms swing at shoulders and elbows,
    reaching and clawing; she breathes and bobs. Charging: arms drawn back and up, the torso rises, the eyes
    blaze, energy gathers at her open mouth - mouth(), where the orbs come from. She stays upright on screen as in
    the art (the rig ignores her heading). A soft magenta halo behind.
  - The shaders take the vertex colour separately (Godot's COLOR already holds the texture - multiplying again had
    squared the colours, magenta turning crimson).
- ProcArt labels "monster_" sprites "Creatures: ...". Docs: game.md (the bio-signature encounter).
- Tests: test_signals 8/8, test_scripts 4/4. Screenshots idle and charging match the reference.
- Files: new tools/skylla_parts.py, shaders/skylla_tentacles.gdshader, shaders/skylla_hair.gdshader,

## 2026-11-08 - The Minotaur fight: playtested, tuned, new weapons, death sequence (all creatures)
- Asked: playtest the boss until killed; then: tougher, rush aimed ahead, a second phase; more diverse weapons
  (a laser beam, a pulse that drains your shields for a few seconds then restores them); orbs and beams from his
  eyes; his shield round his sprite, not over it; beams drawn on top of him; beam and charge aim at the ship and
  then fire at where it was (no tracking while firing); when he dies a shaking animation then a very large
  explosion, only the sprite shaking (no camera shake), the camera centring on him meanwhile and back to the
  player after; the same death sequence for every monster.
- First playtest (scripted fight, starting ship + laser): killed in 39 s, 181 damage taken - too easy.
- Minotaur: hull 5000 (was 1800) + 1500 shields recovering 60/s after 3 s. Attacks in turn (SEQUENCE; phase 2
  below half hull: SEQUENCE_2, orbs 35 % faster, more rushes, shorter pauses):
  - orbs: SpaceMonster's patterns, from his eyes in turn (red and gold);
  - rush: 0.9 s wind-up, a red arrow following you; charges at where you were when it started (980 px/s, 28
    damage, contact within 0.3 x length + your radius - was the hidden sizing ship's radius);
  - beam (new): 0.8 s, a thin line from each eye following you; then twin beams fire along it for 1.8 s, fixed
    (45 dps), drawn above his art;
  - pulse (new): 0.8 s his ring flares; a golden shockwave rolls out (650 px/s to 1500); caught in it, your
    shields go dead for 4 s then come back as they were (Ship.drain_shields / shields_drained).
- Enemy: a creature's shield and hit radius come from SpaceMonster.visual_size() (the art: Skylla 1.96 x 1.25,
  Minotaur 1.43 x length), its shield drawn behind it (glows round the art), a softer hit flash (1.5 not 3).
- Death (SpaceMonster.death_throes, every creature - Skylla, the Minotaur, the Leviathan): 2.4 s of shaking
  (harder and harder, flickering red-hot, explosions bursting across its body), then a 6.5x explosion and four
  more round it; the camera glides onto it (0.6 s) and back to your ship after (0.7 s) - nothing else shakes.
  Enemy._die waits for it before `died` (the quest moves on after the explosion).
- Final playtest (starting ship, pilot dodging): killed in 166 s, no deaths, 820 damage taken; beams always dodged
  by moving off the line; rush hits 4 / 17 (late, when cornered); the drain worked each time; the death sequence
  and the camera return checked in screenshots; the quest ended with its rewards.
- Tests: test_play (20/20, test_minotaur_boss), test_signals 8/8.
- Files: scripts/minotaur_boss.gd, space_monster.gd, sea_witch.gd, enemy.gd, enemy_types.gd, ship.gd
